title: Origins of cells and endosymbiosis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE05a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE05b#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE05b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE05a#N.6, CE05b#N.5, CE05a#N.13b, CE05b#N.9, CE05b#N.12b, CE05b#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ribozymes
items.clue: RNA molecules that act as catalysts

items.label: Stromatolites
items.clue: Layered mats made by bacteria and found as fossils

items.label: Endosymbiosis
items.clue: One organism living inside another, to mutual benefit

items.label: Cyanobacteria
items.clue: Prokaryotes whose photosynthesis produced Earth's oxygenated atmosphere

questions.stem: Earth formed about 4.6 billion years ago (bya), and O₂ began to accumulate in its atmosphere about 2.4 bya. According to the geological and fossil evidence, about when did Earth's environment first become able to support life?

options.text: About 4.6 bya
About 3.5 bya
About 3.9 bya
About 2.4 bya

questions.explanation: Earth formed about 4.6 bya, and its environment was too hostile for life until about 3.9 bya.

questions.stem: Which conclusion is supported by the timeline?

options.text: The first cells could not have existed before 2.4 billion years ago, since all living cells need oxygen.
Life began exactly 3.48 billion years ago, the age of the oldest widely accepted fossils.
Cells existed for at least a billion years before oxygen began to build up in the atmosphere.
The atmosphere held about as much oxygen as it does today when the first fossils formed.

questions.explanation: 3.48 − 2.4 ≈ 1.1 billion years. The earliest life lived without free oxygen.

questions.stem: The RNA world hypothesis proposes that RNA could have been the earliest genetic material. Which property of RNA best explains why RNA, rather than another molecule, is proposed?

options.text: It can store information in its base sequence and can also catalyze reactions.
It can carry information, but only after it is copied into DNA, the genetic material.
It can catalyze reactions, but the information it carries came from early proteins.
It arose because the first cells needed a molecule that could carry their information.

questions.stem: A student claims that photosynthesis by cyanobacteria, which are prokaryotes, produced the oxygenated atmosphere of early Earth. Which of the following provides the best support for this claim?

options.text: Cyanobacteria release more O₂ each year than all the land plants on Earth do today.
Cyanobacteria are simpler than eukaryotes, so they must have photosynthesized first.
Signs of free O₂ first appear in rocks formed when cyanobacteria existed but no eukaryotes did.
Early organisms needed O₂, so cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis in order to make it.

questions.stem: Which observation provides the strongest evidence for the claim that mitochondria evolved from once free-living prokaryotic cells?

options.text: Mitochondria release energy from food molecules, as many free-living bacteria also do.
Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, both resembling those of bacteria.
Mitochondria supply the ATP that large eukaryotic cells need for their many activities.
Eukaryotic cells take in bacteria from their surroundings to form new mitochondria.

questions.stem: Biologists discover a single-celled organism whose cells contain a nucleus, mitochondria and an endoplasmic reticulum, each enclosed by membranes. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: It is the ancestor from which fungi, plants and animals all evolved.
It will in time become a multicellular organism, since it is still primitive.
It is a bacterium, since bacteria are the organisms that are made of a single cell.
It shares an ancestor with fungi, plants and animals that had these organelles.

questions.explanation: Membrane-bound organelles are shared by eukaryotes and indicate their common ancestry, so the organism is a eukaryote that shares a common ancestor with fungi, plants and animals.
